runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: A front-runner's front-runner who should get an uncontested lead over Fontwell's 2m5½f on good ground; his 11 from 15 similar-going efforts and a recent win over this trip make him the natural race-shaper, though he is a ten-year-old handicapper whose trend form (55P31) is mixed and he carries 168lbs for a 3lb conditional.
runners_data.comment: Royal Rhythm arrives here on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with 18 days between runs suggesting he is fit and ready; the chief concern is a pulled-up run two starts back, which clouds his consistency.

runners_data.name: Atreides
runners_data.note: Trainer Neil Mulholland sends him out 18 days fresh wearing a tongue-tie, and though his recent form string (63530) is modest, his prominent style means he is the one horse likely to put Royal Rhythm under at least some pressure; the lack of any win from eight 14-day runs for Mulholland is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and third again four starts back, Atreides brings solid each-way form into this, and 18 days since his last run suggests he returns fresh; he has run over today's trip and a rating of 104 makes him a confident pick despite being yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Jefe Triunfo
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's 7yo returns from a 96-day break — the longest layoff in the field — and his natural hold-up style has worked on good going historically (13 wins/places from 14 sim-going runs), but he has not won from 2019 form and needs real pace to chase down.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 164 lb, Jefe Triunfo has run over today's trip and is well enough regarded on ratings to demand respect, though he is winless in his last five and returns after a 96-day absence.

runners_data.name: County Champs
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who has placed four times on good ground without winning, and last ran just 14 days ago; 2m5½f on good at Fontwell looks squarely in range, but she needs a true gallop to deliver her finish and faces the same traffic problem as the other rear-runners.
runners_data.comment: County Champs has been placed three times in his last five starts — second two runs back, second three runs back, and second five runs back — and returns on a quick turnaround of just 14 days, though the pulled-up effort last time is the obvious concern at 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Clever Relation
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type by nature but pushed into a midfield-on-paper role here because the race has too many hold-up horses to accommodate; his form over 16f rather than today's 21f is a genuine distance query, and Christian Williams has had no 14-day winner from five runners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Clever Relation's recent form includes a pulled-up run and two eighths, making him hard to fancy despite a second two starts back and a fitness edge at just 17 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at five and carrying the minimum 148lbs for James Turner, he is a natural hold-up horse repositioned forward on the map by necessity — his one career placing came over 20f on good, but an Unseated in recent form (06-53U) and a 0 from 6 record for Mrs C Williams in the 14-day window are both caution flags.
runners_data.comment: Kings Order has been winless in his last five starts, including an unseating last time out, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff task under 148 lb, though a third two starts back offers a rare glimmer of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Rhythm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner conditional jockeys' handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest for the lead, Benjamin Macey should be able to dictate a controlled, metronomic gallop over Fontwell's undulating 2m5½f trip. The four hold-up types — Jefe Triunfo, County Champs, Clever Relation and Kings Order — will all be sitting in behind, meaning the closing burst depends heavily on Royal Rhythm either weakening or the pace being strong enough to set up a late challenge. Atreides, the only other prominent-style runner, may push forward to give Royal Rhythm some company but lacks the profile to dominate. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently, control the tempo, and quicken from the front — Royal Rhythm's profile suits perfectly, and true closers face the additional risk that a moderate pace in a small field leaves them with too much to find late. Clever Relation and Kings Order, though genuine hold-up types, have been pushed into the midfield mapping because the race cannot physically accommodate all four rear-runners at the back — both are operating out of their natural zone relative to what the race shape offers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Rhythm Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Rhythm secures the lead unchallenged and sets a comfortable, measured gallop that suits his front-running style.
scenarios.body: Macey settles Royal Rhythm in front, the modest pace draws no serious challenge until the last flight, and a horse that has won over this trip on good going simply has the race run to suit. The small field and lack of a pace rival means stamina is managed perfectly, and Royal Rhythm's recent course form over 20f on good going backs up the profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Rhythm sets a faster-than-expected clip and the race develops into a truly-run stamina test from the front.
scenarios.body: County Champs, a consistent placer over marathon trips on good ground, and Jefe Triunfo, who handles this surface well, get into the race late as Royal Rhythm's lead is eroded in the final half-mile. Both have the stamina pedigree for 2m5½f on a fair surface, though they need tempo to be injected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Duel Late
scenarios.trigger: If Atreides tracks Royal Rhythm closely and turns the final stages into a two-horse battle of the prominent types.
scenarios.body: Atreides has placed at OR 94 with a prominent style and could simply sit a length off Royal Rhythm before launching a challenge at the last; if Royal Rhythm is caught cold by this pressure, Atreides's superior rating relative to the hold-up horses becomes relevant. The closers are left with too much to peg back from midfield if the two prominent types race away.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Reshuffling
scenarios.trigger: If early fallers, unseats or a race incident force a complete tactical reshuffle that negates the front-runner's advantage.
scenarios.body: With Clever Relation and Kings Order bumped out of their preferred hold-up spots and operating at lower-than-natural efficiency, a chaotic scenario could theoretically see these unexposed or fresher horses (Kings Order is only five) profit from a messy race. The probability is low precisely because both are operating out of their true style and their trainer's 14-day record provides no statistical support.

watchPoints.text: Watch Royal Rhythm's early sections — if Benjamin Macey (claiming 3lbs) fails to establish control and Atreides presses him into a faster gallop than intended, the whole race shape flips from front-runner dominance to a stamina slog that reopens the race for County Champs and Jefe Triunfo.

Jefe Triunfo's 96-day absence is the longest in the field; Chris Gordon sends him out fresh and if he jumps well on return he could show more finishing speed than his held-up profile suggests, particularly if the pace is genuine.

Clever Relation and Kings Order are both true hold-up horses forced wide of their natural territory by the field composition — if either is ridden more aggressively than their style suggests, it could create mid-race interference or traffic issues over Fontwell's tight turns.

County Champs ran just 14 days ago and has placed twice over 24f on good going — monitor the market for late Fern O'Brien support, as this runner's reliable placed record on similar ground is the most consistent closer profile in the race.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Maiden Hurdle  (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Anzac Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with OR of 120 but a disappointing recent form string of five successive mid-to-rear finishes; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. gives him a competent pilot but he needs genuine pace to aim at and is unlikely to find it with one uncontested leader in a small field.

runners_data.name: Coastal Command
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's runner represents strong trainer form (1/2 in 14 days) and is the most interesting profile in the race, but 273 days off is a significant query — if fit, his prominent-running style gives him the ideal tactical position to shadow Novelista and pounce.|

runners_data.name: Moab
runners_data.note: The most consistently placed runner in the field with 0W3P from 15 runs on similar going, Brendan Powell takes the ride for Henrietta Knight; ran only 16 days ago so fitness is not a question, but his hold-up style means he needs Novelista to set a proper gallop.|

runners_data.name: Downtown Nashville
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old for Olly Murphy with Sean Bowen aboard, carrying the ⚠ lightly-raced flag; his running style is genuinely unclear from just two hurdles runs but both came on good ground and he placed both times, suggesting he handles conditions — style resolution on the day will be key.|

runners_data.name: Novelista
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's four-year-old is the race's sole confirmed pace-setter and will lead by default; the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 tempers confidence that she can fully capitalise on front-running position, but uncontested control over 2m3f at Fontwell gives her every chance to control the tempo and last home.|

races.paceDynamic: Novelista is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner maiden hurdle over 2m3f at Fontwell, and with no rival likely to press hard for the lead, she will set whatever tempo she chooses from the front. Coastal Command is the other prominent-style runner but arrives after 273 days off and is unlikely to pick a fight for the front, leaving Novelista in full control of the fractions. Downtown Nashville's style is unclear given limited evidence, while Anzac Day and Moab are both held-up types who will be dependent on Novelista not making this too easy for herself. The resulting shape — a single uncontested leader dictating a likely steady-to-moderate gallop over this stamina trip — strongly favours prominent or front-running profiles, and in particular any horse able to travel close to Novelista and produce a clean jumping round, though the hold-up runners will need the pace to lift sufficiently in the final circuit to make their finishing kicks meaningful.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Novelista Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Novelista bowls along uncontested and sets a true-enough gallop that rewards those racing prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Novelista dictates from the front on her own terms, and without pressure she can conserve energy before quickening away from the final hurdle; the runner most likely to profit is whichever prominent tracker can match her jumping and grind on. Coastal Command, if fit enough from a 273-day absence, is best placed to sit in her slipstream and pick up the pieces, while Downtown Nashville's uncertain style means he could also find himself in a useful pressing position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Novelista sets a genuinely honest gallop that strings the field out and the hold-up horses get a strong-enough pace to aim at in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Moab, with the most consistent placed form under similar going conditions and solid placing in recent outings, could be delivered late to challenge if the race develops at sufficient pace to bring his stamina into play. Anzac Day has the highest OR at 120 and hold-up credentials, but his form line shows a string of finishes from fifth to seventh and he needs stronger pace than one uncontested leader typically generates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Tires
scenarios.trigger: If Novelista, racing out of her comfort zone given the STYLE_FIT flag, sets a false gallop before fading and opening the door for a late surge.
scenarios.body: A STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 flags that Novelista may not be entirely comfortable front-running at this level, and if she over-exerts early before weakening, the race fragments late. Moab's consistent placed form and Anzac Day's class on OR could allow a hold-up type to sweep past a strung-out field in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Stuns Field
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at an uneven gallop causing errors or interference that resets the field, allowing a less-fancied runner to capitalise on chaos.
scenarios.body: In a small field over the demanding Fontwell circuit, jumping errors or a stumble by a rival could promote Downtown Nashville or Anzac Day into an unexpected winning position irrespective of pace shape. This is a low-probability disruption scenario, not a pace-driven outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Coastal Command shows any signs of ring-rustiness after 273 days off — if he moves fluently through his hurdles early, his prominent position makes him the most dangerous challenger to Novelista.

Novelista's STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 signals a potential mismatch between her mapped role and natural comfort zone — monitor her jumping and gallop rhythm early; if she labours or makes errors, the hold-up runners will be brought into play much sooner than expected.

Moab has run 16 days ago and arrives with solid placed form, but in a race where pace is likely to be moderate, watch whether Brendan Powell angles for a more prominent position than usual to avoid being left with too much ground to make up.

Downtown Nashville's true running style remains unresolved from a thin form book — Sean Bowen's positioning in the first mile will clarify which scenario is most likely to unfold and could be the decisive tactical factor in a small field.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with genuine course-and-distance form, 4 wins from 15 on similar going, and a sharp 9-day turnaround suggesting he arrives in form; wears a hood and controls this race from flag to finish under Harry Reed — the clear axis of the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Edgewell arrives here just nine days after finishing third, with back-to-back wins three and four starts back underscoring his ability at his best, and he has run over today's trip before; the 168 lb he shoulders is the one query, but our rating has him narrowly on top.

runners_data.name: Gata Ban
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's 9-year-old has won twice over 26f on good ground and arrives 14 days fresh wearing a hood; Dylan Johnston is a capable partner and his hold-up style suits a race where a lone front-runner may leave daylight for a late challenge, though his sim-going record (3 wins from 15) is only fair.
runners_data.comment: Gata Ban arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and a swift 14-day turnaround that suggests she is in the form of her life, with experience over today's trip an added plus; the concern is that a hefty 167 lb burden could blunt her momentum at the death.

runners_data.name: Unspeakable
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes over on this Christian Williams inmate returning from 75 days off; his form includes a 2nd over 26f on good and he handles similar going (2 wins, 5 places from 15 runs), but the layoff is the key risk — he is a hold-up horse who needs things to fall right, which is harder here with so much company from the same position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes of sixth, fourth, sixth and seventh dominating the recent record, Unspeakable also returns from a 75-day absence and our rating of 73 leaves him well below the top of this field — the second five starts back is the lone bright spot, but it is hard to make a strong case here.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: Tracey Leeson's 5-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination — shown in midfield only because the map is congested at the rear; Oscar Palmer claims 7lbs which helps his handicap weight but the redistribution means he is unlikely to get the prominent position that suits him, tempering his chance accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Dual third placings in recent starts underline The Kings Soldier's consistency, and having run over today's trip before, he steps up carrying 147 lb on a quick 17-day turnaround; the concern is he remains winless in his last five and must find another gear to threaten at the finish.

runners_data.name: Frankie Faulkner
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up operator for Mrs C Williams, Adam Wedge takes the ride after a 56-day break; his best form has come on softish ground (2nd and 3rd at 24f on soft) and the current good surface is less ideal — mapped to midfield rather than his preferred rear berth, his positional compromise and going concern combine to make this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Frankie Faulkner shaped with promise when third last time out and has run over today's trip, while our rating of 78 marks him as a genuine threat in this field; the concern is he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 56 days off.

runners_data.name: Of Corse I Can
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's second string, ridden by 3lb claimer Bradley Harris after just 9 days since last run; a consistent if uninspiring hold-up performer (five 4th-to-6th finishes recently) who is at his lowest OR of 69 and carries only 145lbs — genuinely held up at the rear and not in a natural role in the mapped shape, limiting his chance unless the race turns messy.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Of Corse I Can faces a stiff task off 145 lb, though he has run over today's trip before and the quick nine-day turnaround suggests connections believe he retains some form.

races.paceDynamic: Edgewell is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over 3m2f at Fontwell, setting a measured, controllable tempo with no rival willing or able to seriously challenge for the position. Behind him, Gata Ban and Unspeakable are genuine hold-up types who will track from the rear, while The Kings Soldier, Frankie Faulkner, and Of Corse I Can are also natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map — this field holds significantly more off-the-pace types than the shape can accommodate, meaning none of those three is likely to secure a prominent position naturally. With Edgewell dictating a sustainable gallop and no pressure from rivals, he controls the fractions entirely, which classically rewards the leader and any horse capable of travelling close enough to pounce at the second-last. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours Edgewell leading from the front, with any runner who can track him without losing ground through the race — rather than making up ground from deep — best positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edgewell Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell bowls along in front at a fair pace and none of the hold-up brigade can close the gap on the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Edgewell dictates every yard, conserves energy with no challenger, and his strong record at this trip and similar going (4 wins from 15) means he is hard to reel in when fresh and in front; his 9-day turnaround under Nick Scholfield's patient handling suggests he arrives ready.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell's pace proves just slow enough to allow a fresh, well-handicapped hold-up horse to close strongly from the final fence.
scenarios.body: Gata Ban has won twice at this trip on similar going and Dylan Johnston can time a challenge to perfection from the rear; Unspeakable, returning from 75 days off but with a 2nd at this course and distance on good ground, could be sharper than he looks on a flat handicap rating of 78.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses — most likely Frankie Faulkner or The Kings Soldier — pushes forward unexpectedly and forces a contested early pace.
scenarios.body: A more pressured tempo would compress the field and could undermine Edgewell's winning chance if he burns fuel too early, opening the door for a horse with a strong finishing effort; however, with all three redistributed runners carrying a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.93, this scenario demands they race entirely against type.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart at Fences
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a falter at a fence disrupts the lead or causes interference mid-race, scrambling the tactical order.
scenarios.body: A horse like Of Corse I Can, who has been consistent at trips around 21–26f on good ground and carries light weight at 145lbs with a 3lb claimer, could pick through a messy finish; the chaotic shape would suit whoever avoids trouble, not whoever holds the best tactical position.

watchPoints.text: Edgewell has won back-to-back races and arrives 9 days fresh — watch whether Nick Scholfield sends him forward immediately or waits to establish, as early positioning determines whether he gets the uncontested lead his profile depends on.

Gata Ban and Unspeakable are both genuine hold-up horses drawn from the same well — watch how Dylan Johnston and Jack Tudor position them relative to each other, as the two may get in each other's way closing from the rear.

The Kings Soldier, Frankie Faulkner, and Of Corse I Can are all natural hold-up horses who cannot all settle as far back as they prefer — watch the early order for unexpected forward moves from any of them that could disrupt the pace map.

Unspeakable returns from 75 days off and has only raced twice in the last six months — watch his jumping sharpness in the early stages, as a rusty fence could cost him crucial ground he cannot easily recover from a hold-up position.

Of Corse I Can is ridden by a 3lb claimer (Bradley Harris) and races for a trainer (Mulholland) whose 14-day strike rate is 0/8 — watch whether the weight allowance is a genuine compensating factor or merely paper value in a race this horse is unlikely to win from his natural rear position.

races.name: Free Tips Daily On Attheraces.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Start Again
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who sets the pace every time; Fergal O'Brien's stable is 1/9 in the last 14 days and Kielan Woods is a solid booking, though 106 days off the track is a flag and his recent form (P, 6) gives little confidence he can hold on once challenged.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Start Again arrives on a lengthy 106-day break but boasts the strongest profile in this field, our rating of 117 putting him narrowly ahead; he has run over today's trip and carries 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen-ridden prominent racer with solid form credentials including a recent course win; sim-going record of 6/9 (1W, 3P) is encouraging, and 53 days between runs is manageable — the likely chief market rival to No More Bolero from second position.|
runners_data.comment: Ask A Sainte shaped with plenty of promise when a winner three starts back and runner-up two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip at a sturdy 161 lb, with our rating of 112 marking him a leading threat — the sole concern is that pull-up last time out.

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for James Owen, who has a healthy 2/36 strike rate in the 14-day window; four wins from 15 on good ground (best going record here) and back-to-back wins heading into this trip make him the form pick, though a visor headgear flag is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: No More Bolero arrives in fine nick with two wins on the spin and a placed finish on his most recent outing 22 days ago, and he has run over today's trip before; the concern is a hefty 161 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: So Proud
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1W, 2P from 4 sim-going runs) but this five-year-old is a natural prominent type who cannot secure that berth here — expect Jonjo O'Neill Jr. to have to restrain and ride against the horse's instincts, which the STYLE_FIT tag reflects; trainer has 0/12 in the last 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: So Proud shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and a winner four starts back, with a rating of 110 suggesting he retains significant ability; the concern is a 101-day absence that leaves his current fitness open to question.

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Only genuine hold-up horse in the field; Henrietta Knight's runner ran just 9 days ago (a concern for bounce), and his sim-going record on good ground is poor (0W, 2P from 15 runs) — tongue strap fitted, but the evidence does not support him delivering from off a slow pace.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures and held in four of his last five starts, Motazzen is hard to fancy at the weights despite a third last time out and having run over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Start Again is the lone confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the front at what should be a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m3f on good ground — no rival will press him for the lead. Ask A Sainte and No More Bolero are the natural prominent types who will look to sit just behind the leader and travel in a prominent position, while Motazzen will operate from the rear as the only genuine hold-up horse. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — So Proud is a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to claim that spot against Ask A Sainte and No More Bolero, effectively being forced to race in a midfield-to-hold-up role against its nature. With a lone front-runner setting a controlled tempo and two quality prominent horses able to travel in ideal positions just behind, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can dominate a falsely-run or steadily-run contest and strike decisively from the second fence out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Start Again sets a sustainable gallop and the prominent duo track him into contention before striking
scenarios.body: Start Again dictates a comfortable tempo, allowing Ask A Sainte and No More Bolero to travel smoothly in his wake before unleashing their challenges from two out; No More Bolero's excellent recent form (three wins from five on good ground) and Ask A Sainte's strong prominent record make them the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Start Again gets a particularly uncontested lead and the pace stays so controlled that rivals cannot reel him in late
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied and a well-judged Kielan Woods ride from the front, Start Again could pop around economically and simply have too much in reserve; his one win at this trip on good ground and his prominent sim-going record make this a plausible outcome if rivals leave him alone too long.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late or prominent horses use each other up in a bunched finish and Motazzen gets a run
scenarios.body: Motazzen would need an unusually stop-start tempo to deliver a late rattle, and his poor sim-going record (0 wins, 2 places from 15 similar-going runs) makes this a low-probability outcome; a Brendan Powell ride from the back at Fontwell is the only realistic pathway.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Reshuffle Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If So Proud refuses to settle in an unnatural hold-up role and disrupts the race tempo, creating a messy contest
scenarios.body: Racing out of its natural prominent role, So Proud could unsettle the rhythm if it pulls hard or forces rivals wide, opening the door for an unlikely winner; however, with a STYLE_FIT discount and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. needing to manage the situation, this is the least likely scenario.

watchPoints.text: No More Bolero's four wins from 15 good-ground starts is the best sim-going record in the field — watch whether Harry Cobden tracks Start Again from second and strikes two fences out.
Start Again has not run for 106 days and his last two runs read P and 6 — monitor his market move at the off as any drifting price would indicate stable confidence is limited.
So Proud being forced to race off the pace against its natural style is a significant tactical concern — watch whether it settles for Jonjo O'Neill Jr. or pulls hard and wastes energy early.
Motazzen ran just nine days ago; the bounce risk is real for an eight-year-old with a poor good-ground record, and punters should note the tongue strap as a first-time application flag to monitor.

With only five runners, the prominent berths directly behind Start Again are the most valuable real estate in the race — watch the early stalls to see whether Ask A Sainte or No More Bolero claims the better tracking position.

races.name: Free Bets On Attheraces.com Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Three-timer of wins on Good ground over this trip makes him the most dangerous front-runner here; Donald McCain's yard is out of form at 0/15 over 14 days but the horse's own profile is compelling, and he wears a hood (ht) that underlines his need to be kept focused — 61 days off is worth monitoring but his recent form at this track is the key angle.

runners_data.name: Imperial Bede
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill's eight-year-old is 14 days fresh and steps back to this trip having finished placed twice at this distance; 0W in 15 starts on similar going is a concern for win prospects, but his consistent prominent style and Fontwell experience make him a clear place contender if the leaders tire.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Bede has been knocking on the door in recent starts, a second four starts back his most notable effort, and he returns here on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip; winless in his last five, but our rating of 114 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Midnight Jewel
runners_data.note: A decade-old mare fitted with a hood (p) whose last two outings ended in pull-ups, but she was a winner over this trip on Good ground and Charlie Longsdon's small yard has found form with 1 from 3 in 14 days; the question is whether the headgear and an 18-day break have restored enough jumping fluency to sustain her front-running role for the full 2m3½f.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Jewel showed he retains ability with a win in recent starts, and his experience over today's trip and a sharp 18-day turnaround keeps him very much in the mix, though two pulled-up efforts in his last five starts are the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Martin's Denuo
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a live winning run (1114) who holds unexposed potential, but his limited chase form is mainly on Heavy and Soft; David Pipe's in-form yard (1/13 over 14 days) keeps him interesting, though he sits at the rear here largely by default in a pace-heavy field rather than by instinct, and his single Good-ground chase start produced a fourth.
runners_data.comment: Martin's Denuo arrives on the back of three wins in his last five starts and is fit having run just nine days ago, but 155 lb is a stern test of whether he can sustain that sequence.

races.paceDynamic: Jiair Madrik and Midnight Jewel are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off in this small four-runner field, creating an honest, pressured gallop over 2m3½f at Fontwell. Jiair Madrik arrives in excellent form (three consecutive wins) and will look to dictate, while Midnight Jewel — who has headgear listed and was pulled up on her two most recent starts before a return to winning — will push him throughout, ensuring neither can fully control the tempo. Imperial Bede has shown prominent tendencies and will sit close to the pace, leaving Martin's Denuo — a lightly-raced, redistributed type — to drift rearward by default rather than genuine hold-up preference. This race shape, with two front-runners pressing each other, most favours a well-positioned prominent racer who can travel comfortably just off the contested lead and pick up the pieces if the front pair weaken; the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions, with Jiair Madrik and Midnight Jewel the most likely to actually lead, leaving Imperial Bede fighting for a pitch just behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Grind Each Other
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik and Midnight Jewel press each other relentlessly, burning each other out before the final two fences.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel drains both leaders, opening the door for the horse travelling most comfortably in behind; Imperial Bede, a consistent Fontwell performer over this trip, is ideally placed to capitalise by staying on at the one pace as the front pair fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Jiair Madrik Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik asserts quickly enough to force Midnight Jewel off the bridle early and effectively controls the pace solo from the front.
scenarios.body: With Midnight Jewel unable to sustain the challenge, Jiair Madrik is freed to dictate a rhythm that suits his stamina, and his three-timer of wins on Good ground at this trip underpins his credentials to go clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midnight Jewel Revives
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Jewel bounces back under her headgear (p) and outstays Jiair Madrik in the closing stages after matching him stride for stride.
scenarios.body: Her most recent win was over this sort of distance and on Good ground, and if the headgear sharpens her jumping and focus she has the class off OR 104 to hold on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Improver Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Martin's Denuo, a young and lightly-raced chaser, finds the strongly-run pace suit his stamina and comes through beaten rivals in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Martin's Denuo is not a natural hold-up type but his age, lightly-raced profile and recent winning run give him a chance if the front runners capitulate; however, this scenario requires him to race out of role and is the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Midnight Jewel's jumping must be monitored — two consecutive pull-ups suggest a repeat jumping error could end her race early and significantly alter the dynamic if the front-running duel becomes uncontested.

Jiair Madrik and Midnight Jewel pressing each other from the off in a four-runner field is the central risk factor; if either capitulates before three out, watch whether Imperial Bede has enough petrol left from tracking them to win rather than just place.

Martin's Denuo's youth and inexperience over fences on Good ground is a live danger — a blunder or jumping hesitancy at Fontwell's quirky track layout could end his challenge before the race truly develops.

Donald McCain's 0/15 trainer strike rate over the past 14 days is a form-line flag on Jiair Madrik despite the horse's personal form being strong — worth watching in-running for any signs he is not fully wound up after 61 days off.
With only four runners, any incident (fall, unseated, pull-up) radically reshapes the race; the field is so small that the loss of even one runner transforms the tactical picture entirely.

runners_data.name: Lady Chauntee
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore completely unexposed, Lady Chauntee arrives with her cards firmly to her chest on debut, carrying 156 lb, and there is every reason to keep her onside as she has shown nothing to rule her out of contention.

runners_data.name: Milliedram
runners_data.comment: Milliedram has run over today's trip and brings solid ability into this, her rating of 82 making her a genuine threat in this field, though 116 days off the track is the chief concern for a mare yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Uptoyourselves
runners_data.comment: Uptoyourselves won on her most recent start, with a pull-up three starts back the only real blemish in a lightly raced profile that leaves her open to further improvement; 133 days between runs is the main query under 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Delulu
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, Delulu arrives here in fine fettle after just a fortnight's break, with a trainer firing at a striking 33% strike rate over the past 14 days; she's yet to win in recent starts, but our top rating of 105 makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Main De Fer
runners_data.comment: Unraced and completely unexposed, Main De Fer arrives on debut carrying 154 lb, an open-to-improvement unknown whose potential remains entirely to be seen.

runners_data.name: Petite Poet
runners_data.comment: Petite Poet shapes as a leading threat on our rating despite being yet to score in her last two starts, and having run over today's trip she arrives with relevant experience; the main concern is her 44-day absence.

runners_data.name: Silver Whisper
runners_data.comment: Silver Whisper shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, has run over today's trip, and her rating of 92 makes her a genuine threat to the top pair; the concern is she has been off the track for 105 days and remains yet to score.
